version.value: Berg’s Lyric Suite for string quartet (the 1926 quartet version); the edition used by the performers is not stated.
version.note: The Internet Archive description gives the title and “for string quartet (1926)”; the advertisement of 1937 gives “Suite Lyrique. For String Quartet”. The movement is the third of six; the file runs 3:42 and carries the whole movement.

value.name: Adrienne Galimir (spelled “Adrielle” in the item description)

performers.note: The advertisement names the “Galimir String Quartet of Vienna”. The item description lists the four players. The second violinist’s name is “Adrielle” there and Adrienne in the Boston Symphony Orchestra note, which says the quartet consisted of a brother and three sisters.

date.note: Stated in the item description (“Recorded c. 1935-36”). Wikipedia’s list of recordings gives “ca. 1935”; no session ledger was seen.

place.note: Stated in the item description, which says the recording was made “for French Polydor”. The label of the American disc 95007 reads “Recorded in France”.

label.note: The item description lists the three issues and adds a reissue by Vox in July 1948. The March 1937 advertisement shows the American issue by Brunswick-Polydor.

catalogue.value: Brunswick-Polydor set BP No. 2 (records 95006–95009; slide-automatic set BP-2A, 95010–95013); earlier issues Polydor 516.659–516.662 and Decca CA-8244–8247 as given in the item description
catalogue.note: The set number BP No. 2 is confirmed by the March 1937 advertisement and by the label photograph of disc 95007; the Polydor and Decca numbers and the British issue date (December 1936) are from the item description only. Wikipedia’s list of recordings gives the first issue as Polydor 595.135–595.138; the two sets of numbers were not reconciled.

matrixTakeSides.value: Brunswick-Polydor 95007, “In 8 Parts”, Part III, with the third movement named on the label; matrix and take numbers are not given
matrixTakeSides.note: Read from the label photograph in the Internet Archive item (“Part III … Set No. BP-2 … Third Movement: Allegro misterioso”). The item description and the label give no matrix or take numbers. The files are labelled (i) to (vi), one for each movement.

credits.value: Internet Archive collection shellackophile-recordings; no individual transfer credit
credits.note: The item names a collection but no transfer engineer.

date.value: Not stated; the item was made public on 13 March 2022
date.note: The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

processing.value: Each movement is one file, uploaded as FLAC with an MP3 derivative; equalisation and noise reduction are not described.
processing.note: The published MP3 is the Internet Archive derivative.

digital.format: Internet Archive derivative VBR MP3 from an uploaded FLAC

composition.value: Berg died in 1935, so the work has been in the public domain in the EU and other life-plus-70 countries since 2006. Its United States status is not assessed here.
composition.note: Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; the American issue was advertised by March 1937.
recording.note: The item description gives earlier French and British issues, which were not checked in a second source. The United States status of a recording made in France in the 1930s is not established.

rights.creditLine: Alban Berg, Lyric Suite, III. Galimir String Quartet of Vienna. Recorded c. 1935–36; issued as Brunswick-Polydor set BP No. 2, advertised in March 1937. Internet Archive item bp-2-berg-suite-lyrique-iv (collection shellackophile-recordings). Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established.
